event: Sunday: you wake at six on your own, and you know where you're going before you're up.
The fisherman's jumper over knickers and bra again; the shore grey and silent.
Shiv is on the rock, peeling off her socks; she looks up, and this time she just smiles.
You go in together off the edge, hand in hand; the cold is still a fist, but you breathe out.
Two minutes this time, treading water face to face, the mist lifting off the mere around you.

memory.fact: On Sunday at dawn Nala swam with Shiv again for two minutes, breathing out through the cold.
On Sunday at dawn Nala swam with Shiv again for two minutes, breathing out through the cold.

event: On the rock, wrapped in her parka, your teeth chattering, Shiv puts her cold hands on your face.

pictured.coverAfter: On the rock she wraps you in her parka again. She zips it to your chin

event: "Still might," she says, and you say, "Then do," and she kisses you.

memory.fact: On the rock on Sunday, Shiv said still might, Nala said then do, and Shiv kissed her.
On the rock on Sunday, Shiv said still might, Nala said then do, and Shiv kissed her.

event: Her mouth is cold and then warm, tasting of the mere; your whole burning body goes quiet under it.
It's your first kiss in this body; your lips feel twice as many things as they ever did before.

memory.fact: Shiv's kiss on the rock was Nala's first kiss in her new body.

event: She pulls back, grinning now, freckles beaded with water: "Grand. That's settled, then."
You tell her again there are others you want; she says she remembers, and kisses you again.

memory.fact: Told again that Nala wants others too, Shiv said she remembers, and kissed her again.
Told again that Nala wants others too, Shiv said she remembers, and kissed her again.

event: Hot shower; you touch your mouth in the steamed mirror, and laugh at yourself out loud.

pictured.coverAfter: In the late morning you go down to the laundry.

event: Late morning: laundry in Thornfield's cellar, three washers, two dryers, and a Sunday queue.

memory.fact: Thornfield's laundry room is in the cellar: three washers, two dryers, and a queue every Sunday.

event: Bea is in the queue with a basket; she teaches you which things can't go in the dryer.
Bras on the airer, she says, never the dryer, and holds one of yours up, and you both crack up.

memory.fact: Bea taught Nala to sort her laundry: wool and bras never go in the dryer.
Bea taught Nala to sort her laundry: wool and bras never go in the dryer.

event: She looks at you properly, then: your mouth, your glow. "Something's happened," she says.
You tell her: Shiv, the rock, a kiss. Bea goes still, then says she's glad, a bit too brightly.

memory.fact: On the rock on Sunday, Shiv said still might, Nala said then do, and Shiv kissed her.
On Sunday at dawn Nala swam with Shiv again for two minutes, breathing out through the cold.

event: She busies herself with the washer for a long minute; you see her blink hard.

memory.fact: Told of Shiv's kiss, Bea said she was glad, too brightly, then blinked back tears at the washer.
Told of Shiv's kiss, Bea said she was glad, too brightly, then blinked back tears at the washer.

event: One o'clock: Sunday roast in the Great Hall, beef and gravy, the last hot food until Monday.

memory.fact: On Sundays the Great Hall serves a roast at one, and nothing else hot until breakfast.

event: Group F ends up at one table; Amara and Kit sit opposite each other by pure bad luck.
They spar over their shared essay question, politely savage, across the gravy boat.
You ask them each what they actually think; for a moment they both answer honestly.

memory.fact: Amara says her grandmother's ring, a held focus, remembers every spell it has helped make.
Amara says her grandmother's ring, a held focus, remembers every spell it has helped make.
Amara says her grandmother's ring, a held focus, remembers every spell it has helped make.
Amara says her grandmother's ring, a held focus, remembers every spell it has helped make.

event: They find they disagree on exactly one point and agree on everything else, which annoys them both.

memory.fact: Kit and Amara agree on their essay but for one point: whether a focus remembers, or is worn.
Kit and Amara agree on their essay but for one point: whether a focus remembers, or is worn.
Kit and Amara agree on their essay but for one point: whether a focus remembers, or is worn.

event: Shiv sits down beside you with a full plate, bumps your knee under the table, and says nothing.
Lin, across the table, sees the knee bump, and looks at her plate, thoughtful and calm.

memory.fact: At Sunday roast Shiv sat by Nala and rested her knee against Nala's under the table; Lin saw.
At Sunday roast Shiv sat by Nala and rested her knee against Nala's under the table; Lin saw.

event: Afternoon: the boathouse lends rowing boats on Sundays; Bea signs one out and takes the oars.

memory.fact: The boathouse on the academy shore lends rowing boats to students on Sunday afternoons.

event: She rows like she was born doing it, long clean strokes, out into the middle of the mere.

pictured.coverAfter: Shiv. Her hair is damp and curling and she's in her grey hoodie, and her plate

event: She stops, oars dripping, the fells all round you; the academy small and far on the shore.
"Can I be honest?" she says. "When you said about Shiv, it went in me like a splinter."

memory.fact: Rowing Nala out on the mere, Bea told her Shiv's kiss went in her like a splinter.
Rowing Nala out on the mere, Bea told her Shiv's kiss went in her like a splinter.

pictured.coverAfter: It's down on the academy shore, past Shiv's rock, a long low wooden building

event: You tell her the truth: wanting Shiv takes nothing from wanting to be near her; it never would.

memory.fact: Nala told Bea that wanting Shiv takes nothing from wanting to be near her, and never would.
Nala told Bea that wanting Shiv takes nothing from wanting to be near her, and never would.

event: Bea says she doesn't know yet what she wants with you, but she knows she wants to be in your boat.
"You're in my boat," you say. She laughs, wet-eyed, and splashes you with an oar.

memory.fact: Bea said she doesn't know yet what she wants with Nala, but wants to be in her boat; Nala: you are.
Bea said she doesn't know yet what she wants with Nala, but wants to be in her boat; Nala: you are.

event: She lets you try rowing; you go in a slow circle; she laughs so hard the boat rocks.

memory.fact: Trying to row, Nala only went in circles, and Bea laughed until the boat rocked.
Trying to row, Nala only went in circles, and Bea laughed until the boat rocked.

event: Evening: the library is open till midnight on Sundays; you take your essay and the new pen.

memory.fact: The library opens at noon on Sundays and stays open until midnight.

event: Kit is at the far end of a green-lamped table, alone; she moves her books to make room for you.
You work in silence for an hour; it's the easiest silence you've had since you arrived.

memory.fact: Kit made room for Nala at her library table on Sunday night, and they worked an hour in silence.
Kit made room for Nala at her library table on Sunday night, and they worked an hour in silence.

event: Kit asks to see your paragraph; she reads it twice. "This is good," she says. "Annoyingly."
She says Penhallow will like that you wrote it, not what you read; you glow.

memory.fact: Kit read Nala's paragraph twice and called it good, annoyingly; Penhallow will like it, she said.
Kit read Nala's paragraph twice and called it good, annoyingly; Penhallow will like it, she said.
Kit's grandmother said Dr Penhallow always wants what happened to you, not what books said.

event: Walking out at ten, Kit asks, very offhand, whether you'd go to the cinema again sometime.
You say yes; she nods once, sharply, and leaves for Ashcombe before you can see her face.

memory.fact: Kit asked Nala, very offhand, to go to the cinema again sometime, and Nala said yes.
Kit asked Nala, very offhand, to go to the cinema again sometime, and Nala said yes.

event: Thornfield kitchen: cold supper, toast and cheese; Bea's there, and Lin up from downstairs.
Lin gives you a small twist of paper: one of the old nibs from Kendal, cleaned and polished.
"It's soft," she says. "Like the one I lent you. It's yours now." You hold it like treasure.

memory.fact: Lin cleaned and polished a soft old nib from Kendal, and gave it to Nala to keep.
Lin cleaned and polished a soft old nib from Kendal, and gave it to Nala to keep.

event: Bea makes three teas without asking anyone, bumps your shoulder, and her smile is real again.
In bed, your mouth still remembering the mere, you think: one kiss, five girls, and Monday.
